question.text: Three point charges of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> are located at the vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></math> of a right angled triangle whose sides are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is the right angle corner. Charge at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> experiences _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> of electrostatic force due to the other two charges.

solution.text:
Using Coulomb's law the electrostatic force on A due to C

FAC=KqAqCrAC2=k×5×0.3×10-129×10-4=9×109×5×0.3×10-129×10-4

=1.5×10=15 N

Similarly, the force on A due to B

FAB=KqAqBrAB2=9×109×5×0.16×10-129×10-4=8 N

We can see that the forces are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the net force experienced by charge at A is,

F=FAC2+FAB2=152+82=289=17 N
